title: Residual arithmetic and cancellation qualification at G21L balance boundaries
question: Are the B2 total-balance split and B1 node-4 compartment split explainable by binary64 aggregation order/cancellation of the already-computed HeadCalc residual terms, or do the threshold classifications survive independent exact-float and compensated recombination?

separation.arm_b2: Full final residual-vector aggregation at B2 status-0/status-6 heads.
separation.arm_b1: Final node-4 residual expression term aggregation at the B1 status-6 head, with the adjacent status-0 state as control.
not_claimed: That stable aggregation proves absence of floating-point sensitivity inside constitutive, storage, gradient or conductivity term construction.
That higher-precision diagnostic arithmetic should replace production binary64 arithmetic.
That any observed cancellation justifies changing solver tolerances.
That G21 dynamic path equivalence is restored.

frozen_source.compiler_contract: existing FGC44 research semantic build flags; no fast-math option

research_build_instrumentation.rule: Generate a temporary copy of HeadCalc from the pinned production blob and insert a read-only call immediately after the existing sump, sum1 and Fmax calculations. The call records the already-computed residual vector and separately materialized node-4 expression terms. Do not modify any committed src/** file.
research_build_instrumentation.observer_semantics: overwrite research scratch on every Newton iteration; after HeadCalc returns the snapshot is therefore the final evaluated iteration. Read only after the frozen prefix solve.

independent_arithmetic_contract: Recover every final residual component as its binary64 value and require the native vector, sum and Fmax to reproduce G21L.

For each residual vector compute ordinary left-to-right binary64 sum, reverse-order binary64 sum, every permutation sum for four components, Python math.fsum, and a high-precision Decimal sum constructed exactly from each binary64 input.
Classify whether abs(total residual) > 1e-12 is invariant over all these recombinations. Do not change the residual components themselves.
For B1 node 4 recover the six signed expression terms and repeat ordinary, reverse, every-permutation, math.fsum and exact-binary64 Decimal recombination.
Require the recorded node-4 native residual to reproduce G21L. Separately report whether its >1e-12 classification is invariant under recombination of the already-rounded terms.
Compute cancellation ratio=sum(abs(terms))/abs(exact sum) for B1 node 4 and sum(abs(residual_i))/abs(exact vector sum) for each vector.

If a classification crosses 1e-12 under permitted recombination, classify AGGREGATION_ORDER_SENSITIVE. If it is invariant, classify AGGREGATION_ORDER_NOT_CAUSAL_AT_CAPTURED_TERM_LEVEL; do not extrapolate that statement upstream.
gates: Pinned production HeadCalc blob matches and contains no G21M observer.
Full existing FGC44 end-to-end and G21L gates pass in the research build.
All four frozen solver-status/backtracking tuples reproduce.
Recorded native residual vectors reproduce G21L sum/max values to binary64 equality where the same native operations are recorded.
B2 status-6 and status-0 aggregation classifications are reported prospectively from all recombination methods.
B1 node-4 native residual reproduces G21L and its recombination classification is reported prospectively.
No committed src/** or standard FGC44 bridge source changes.
Normal G16 diagnostic non-authority postconditions remain unchanged.
pass_interpretation: PASS determines whether final aggregation order/cancellation of already-computed binary64 residual components or node terms is sufficient to explain the observed threshold flips. A stable result narrows any remaining floating-point mechanism to upstream term construction or nonlinear path sensitivity; it does not prove exact-real arithmetic equivalence.
fail_interpretation: Preserve any aggregation-order sensitivity or reconstruction mismatch. Do not alter term grouping, compiler flags, tolerances, frozen heads or solver prefixes after seeing the result.
